newsitem.title: ERITREA: Eritrea assembly holds first session.
newsitem.headline: Eritrea assembly holds first session.

text.p: Eritrea's single-party transitional assembly has held its first session, one week after the constitution was ratified, a senior government official said on Tuesday.
The main task facing the 150-seat assembly, which met on Friday, is to prepare for elections, Zemhret Yohannes of the ruling People's Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ) told Reuters.
"At the meeting...we decided to establish a committee to draft electoral laws," said Zemhret, PFDJ head of documentation and research.
Electoral laws would be presented at the next meeting in five months but elections would take "more than one year" to organise, he said.

The PFDJ is the renamed former guerrilla movement the Eritrean People's Liberation Front (EPLF), which won a 30-year independence war against Ethiopia in 1993. Half of the transitional assembly members were elected at an EPLF congress in 1994.
President Isaias Afewerki proclaimed the country's first constitution on May 24, independence day.
